headline: JIBEX opens in Jeddah with a China pavilion and Mobedex alongside
deck: The building exhibition runs three days with Mobedex alongside, covering materials, equipment and stone for Jeddah's contractor base.
excerpt: JIBEX opens at Jeddah's exhibition centre on 15 September with Mobedex running alongside, a sponsored China pavilion and an exhibitor list weighted toward building materials.
content:
The Jeddah International Building Exhibition opens at the Jeddah Centre for Exhibitions and Events on 15 September, running to 17 September with evening hours of 16:00 to 22:00 and the Mobedex interiors show running concurrently. It is organised by Icon International with KAC.

JIBEX covers building materials, construction equipment and tools, electricity and lighting, safety, security and fire, water technology, waste management, engineering consultancies, and marble, granite and stone. Mobedex takes furniture, paints, doors and windows, hotel equipment, flooring, smart home technology, curtains and home textiles. Participating countries are given as Saudi Arabia, China, Egypt and Jordan.

The sponsor list is specific. Saudi Red Bricks holds the diamond position and Petromin Foton silver, with CBGG and Zhejiang as official sponsors of the China pavilion, Reef as co-sponsor and Roznamah as media partner. Named exhibitors include Al-Diyar Al-Mubtakarah, BATCO, Unique Scaffolding, Abwab Aman, SIPOREX, Rose Paints, Marmox, El-Dowegry, Sika, Professional Glass, Diamond Glass and Rock Door.

The China pavilion, with two dedicated sponsors behind it, is the most substantial single block on the roster. Chinese building materials suppliers have been increasing their Saudi presence steadily, and a sponsored national pavilion at a Jeddah show is a distribution play aimed at the western region's contractors. SIPOREX, Sika and Marmox on the same list represent the established specification end of the same market.

The western region is a sensible target for the format. Jeddah has fewer competing building exhibitions than Riyadh, its contractor base is oriented toward residential and commercial work rather than giga-projects, and Jeddah Islamic Port makes import logistics straightforward for exhibitors bringing product in.

The stone and marble category deserves particular note. Saudi Arabia has substantial domestic stone resources and a long-established cutting and finishing trade, and the western region carries much of it. It is one of the building material categories where local supply competes on quality rather than only on freight cost.

Evening hours suit a trade audience attending after their own working day, and reflect a buyer profile weighted toward owners, small contractors and independent specifiers rather than corporate procurement teams.

Exhibitor, sponsor and category detail is taken from the organiser's published material. Exhibitor and visitor figures for the 2026 edition are expected closer to the opening. This publication has reported the wider Saudi building materials market, including the movement of international construction chemicals manufacturers toward regional production.

Mobedex runs concurrently, taking furniture, paints, doors and windows, hotel equipment, flooring, smart home technology, curtains and home textiles. Together the two cover the building envelope and its interior, which suits a visitor working across both.
